items: Verify Before Acting: Ask the three key questions honestly: What exactly was said? What exactly was yours? Was intent present? Answering these prevents acting on misinterpretation and gives you legitimate ground to stand on.

Verify Before Acting: Complete the Credit Audit Worksheet in writing, separating facts from interpretations, because writing it out forces you to distinguish what actually happened from how you're currently feeling.
Verify Before Acting: Identify one specific contribution nobody can dispute to anchor yourself when self-doubt starts questioning your own value and making you wonder if the theft even happened.

Verify Before Acting: Wait 24 hours before responding if you're uncertain, because clarity often comes once the initial sting fades and you can think more clearly about whether the situation warrants action.
Build Your Documentation: Send follow-up emails after meetings where you contributed key points to create a timestamped record that proves you were present and what you added to the conversation.
Build Your Documentation: Reply-all to emails where credit is being discussed to restate your specific contribution clearly and create written documentation that will be hard to dispute later.
Build Your Documentation: Keep a running log of meetings, your contributions, and decisions made in each one to build a pattern of evidence showing your involvement over time.
Build Your Documentation: Document each incident with the date, context, what was said, and what you contributed so you have facts ready if you need to escalate or have a conversation later.
Respond Strategically: Prepare a calm, factual response for when it happens again so you're not caught off guard and scrambling for words in the moment when emotions are running high.

Respond Strategically: Reply to the thread where your work was claimed with a statement like 'Building on my earlier analysis...' to reassert your contribution without making accusations or creating conflict.

Respond Strategically: Have a private debrief with your manager where you calmly present the facts and request clarification rather than accusation, because this approach preserves relationships while protecting you.
Respond Strategically: Decide what outcome you want before entering any conversation about credit theft so you stay focused on your goal rather than getting sidetracked by defensiveness or emotion.
